results.reason: R1.6's migration override list is stale after the stereotype collapse — it names two stereotypes that no longer exist and omits MassTransit's third override.
results.expected: R1.6: the module documentation lists EVERY MassTransit name override a migrator must re-apply, naming correctly where each now lives, so an override that is not re-applied cannot silently fall back to the convention-derived destination.
results.actual: docs/README.md:264 maps MassTransit's `Entity Name` to `Message Topology Settings` -> `Topic Name` and asserts 'Same stereotype name and same attachment point - carries across directly'. docs/README.md:265 names `Command Distribution` -> `Destination Queue Name`. BOTH stereotypes were deleted by the heal: `Topic Name` and `Destination Queue Name` now live on the single `Wolverine Message` stereotype (292b1227-a311-4bc1-bbf5-5f0ba070b0b1), applyMode manually, and the template reads only GetWolverineMessage()?.TopicName() / .DestinationQueueName(). A migrator following either row re-applies nothing and silently gets the convention-derived destination - exactly the failure R1.6's last sentence exists to prevent. MassTransit's third override, `Command Consumption` -> `Queue Name`, is absent from the table entirely, even though it has no Wolverine equivalent (subscriber queue names are not overridable in this release) and is therefore precisely an override a migrator must be told is lost. Adjacent defect, same root cause: docs/README.md:217 states 'There is no per-message handler registration to remove, because none is generated in the first place' - false since the module now emits one opts.Discovery.IncludeType<T>() per subscribed message.
results.location: Modules/Intent.Modules.Eventing.Wolverine/docs/README.md - lines 264 and 265 (the two override rows), the missing `Command Consumption` -> `Queue Name` row, and line 217 in the Uninstalling section.

results.reason: R18.1's second responsibility - the call that disables Wolverine's conventional handler discovery - is emitted nowhere.
results.expected: R18.1: the Shared Host Module owns BOTH the Wolverine host registration AND the call that disables conventional handler discovery, and no other Wolverine module emits either.
results.actual: No DisableConventionalDiscovery, CustomizeHandlerDiscovery or equivalent exists in Intent.Modules.Wolverine.Common, Intent.Modules.Eventing.Wolverine or Intent.Modules.Application.Wolverine, and no generated output under Tests/ contains one. Discovery is deliberately left enabled: WolverineHostRegistrationExtension.cs:121 emits opts.Discovery.IncludeAssembly(...), and each module now adds its own opts.Discovery.IncludeType<T>() (Eventing: WolverineEventingConfigurationTemplatePartial.cs:621; Application.Wolverine: WolverineConfigurationTemplatePartial.cs:51,58). IMPORTANT CONTEXT: this is a DELIBERATE USER DECISION taken during the heal - the user chose explicit handler-type registration WITHOUT disabling conventional discovery. The anti-stranding hazard R18.1 guards against is genuinely addressed by a different mechanism (one additive UseWolverine lambda whose statements may never be cleared, plus per-owner explicit registrations), but that is a weaker guarantee than explicit-only registration, and the specific call R18.1 names does not exist. R18.2, R18.4, R18.5 and R18.6 all verify clean (one UseWolverine per host confirmed per-application; Application.Wolverine contributes via WolverineHostConfigurationRequest; eventing works with no CQRS module installed; GOLDEN-SAMPLE: sweep returns nothing). Also still open under R18.3: Intent.Application.Wolverine.DomainEvents registers none of its own handler types, so the blanket IncludeAssembly cannot yet be removed and registrations are additive-per-owner rather than exclusively per-owner.
results.location: Resolve by EITHER emitting the disable call from Modules/Intent.Modules.Wolverine.Common/FactoryExtensions/WolverineHostRegistrationExtension.cs (~line 121) OR amending requirements R18.1/R18.3 to describe the additive-registration mechanism actually built. Do not silently pick one - this needs the user's decision, which they have already leaned against once. Separately, Intent.Application.Wolverine.DomainEvents needs its own handler-type registrations before the blanket IncludeAssembly can go.

results.actual: git ls-files counts: WolverineEventing.Publish.RabbitMQ 166, WolverineEventing.Subscribe.RabbitMQ 154, CompositeMessageBus 304 tracked. Nothing in .gitignore blocks them (git check-ignore returns rc=1); they are simply uncommitted. Six of those apps additionally hold an ORPHANED DUPLICATE tree at Tests/X/Tests/X totalling ~435 files (73 each for the four ErrorPolicy apps and Outbox.SqlServer.Publish, 70 for Outbox.SqlServer.Subscribe), left behind when the doubled output locations were corrected; all untracked, and they inflate those apps' file counts with junk. Traceability carries 11 unresolved file targets belonging to applications withdrawn from the matrix: T9.1 (Transport.Local, 2), T9.5 (Topology.ExternallyOwned, 2), T10.2 (Outbox.Postgresql Publish and Subscribe, 4) and T11.2 (MultiProvider, 3). The .gitignore un-ignore block for Tests/Wolverine.Transport.Local/ now refers to an application that does not exist. Behaviour is otherwise sound and should NOT be re-done: all 13 applications build with 0 errors, and the six relocated apps each re-run the Software Factory with zero proposed changes (R19.3 holds for them).
results.location: Delete the six orphaned Tests/*/Tests/* duplicate trees; commit the generated output for the ten untracked applications under Tests/; remove the dead .gitignore un-ignore block for Tests/Wolverine.Transport.Local/ (around line 254); and re-record traceability for tasks T9.1, T9.5, T10.2 and T11.2, whose matrix rows were withdrawn from R19.1.
